posts.name: DerpTheBugbear
posts.cooked:
Dunno if I'm doing this right, I assume you can pick any hero/villain combination that hasn't been done yet?  If so, here's the game I played earlier today!  Sorry if this is a little overly detailed.  :-P
 
 
Dark Watch Vs. Chairman At Pike Industrial
Or
RATS!!  RATS EVERYWHERE!!!!
 
 
The Darkwatch,  A team formed to combat evil in the darkest corners of the world and beyond.  And what darker place is there than the Underworld of Rook City's criminal society? 
 
The recent disappearance of various museum pieces, which are believed to be linked to an old forgotten ritual, had not gone unnoticed by the arcane investigator known as 'Nightmist'.  In record time, she had tracked the thief down to a certain fence known for having connections to Chairman Pike.  After taking the thief out and examining the stolen object she realized that Pike was intending to perform a ritual for immortality and god-like power!!
 
Upon this discovery Nightmist called upon the rest of the Nightwatch...  Chairman Pike must be stopped at all costs!
 
Villain:
The Chairman
 
Environment:  
Pike Industrial
 
Heroes:
Dark-Watch Setback
Dark-Watch Expatriette
Dark-Watch Mr. Fixer
Dark-Watch Nightmist
 
 
Chairman Pike and his Operative started off with a few Undivided Attentions, dealing a crapload of damage right out the gate.  After that it was relatively slow.  You had your typical 1 Underboss per round from Operative, which eventually brought out more thugs.  Both Prison breaks ended up being at the very bottom of the deck, so they came out one after another, AFTER all the underbosses had been killed.  So we suddenly had a LOT of targets out in play at once.  Other than that, nothing too abnormal happened with the villain deck.
 
Pike Industrial had some early game vat explosions help take out some thugs and underbosses.  Setback used Cash Out to heal some of the influx of damage from the explosions.  near the end of the game we got 2 Irradiated Cyclohexane Vats out boosting all damage by 2.  It was at that time that the Prison Breaks occured. We had rats coming out every so often up till that point, and they were all in the trash.  Then of course we got the experimental mutagens to bring out all the rats and boosting their damage, which ended up helping clear out the prison break. (at this point, we had around 14 non-hero targets in play) 
 
 
Setback applied a liberal use of Mitigate throughout the game and Cashed Out at opportune moments to provide healing to the rest of the team.  He really didn't draw the best combination of cards throughout the game, which was unfortunate.  He was the first to be incapacitated, which actually helped by allowing Ex-Pat and Fixer to use powers more often.
 
Ex-Pat was a steady stream of damage.  She got an assault rifle, speed loading, and 2 copies of hollowpoints early on. and a shotgun for single target hits.  This let her hit 3 targets per round for 4 damage (before other dmg+'s) which really helped keep thugs and underbosses out of play. She never really had much time to even use Aim.  She was incapacitated second, at which point Fixer was allowed to use bitter strike 3 times in one round (which ate up a LOT of equipment).
 
Mr Fixer used his wrench most of the game for the bonus to damage and defense, destroying styles with bitter strike.  He eventually got bloody knuckles, jackhandle, and alternating tiger claw  out all at the same time to deal a ton of irreducable to every non-hero target shortly after both prison breaks went off, to nearly clear the board.  He also got a really well timed Grease Gun out that kept Setback and Ex-pat alive for one extra turn so they could do more damage before dying. He was incapacitated last.
 
Nightmist was in and out of Mist form for most of the game.  with some lucky shuffling/draws, she seemed to always have it as an option.  Her biggest contribution was her amulet of elder gods, which allowed her to redirect some pretty nasty hits towards the Operative and later, the Chairman. Near the end, after the prison break and mutated rat swarm were dealt with by Fixer's amazing combo, she popped Mist-Fueled Recovery with 18+ cards in her discard to heal back up to full health.  
 
At this point all that was left on the board was Nightmist (at near full health), and the Chairman (at around 10 health).  She was preparing to nuke Pike utilizing her hand which comprised half her deck at this point, However, an unexpected second round of Mutated Rats poured out onto the field, devouring The Chairman and taking a sizable chunk out of Nightmist!
(Chairman is immune to environment damage, but since he was doomed at this point, I like to imagine that it ended this way)

At a weekend trip full of tobacco, whiskey, and gaming, I introduced some friends to Sentinels and probably got them hooked - they were asking about price when we were getting ready to leave.

 

A lot of these combinations have already been done or mostly done, but I added a few.  Some of these were player choice (Oooh that guy/girl sounds interesting!) and some were completely random.

 

Voss in Insula Primalis (the introductory game for the new people) vs. The Sentinels, Fanatic, Ex-patriette, Omnitron-X, and Mr. Fixer.  There were a few comments of "This is supposed to be an easy intro game?" due to one of the flagships and two enraged T-Rex's, but overall it was fine, of course.  Never did get to show them the potential horror of Forced Deployment.

Gloomweaver in the Realm of Discord for some folks who've played SotM before but not that villain, squaring off against Unity, Absolute Zero, and the Argent Adept.  Pretty much a cakewalk.

Ambuscade ambushed the team of Parse, Tachyon, Bunker and the Scholar in the Ruins of Atlantis.  Again there was some disbelief when I said that Ambuscade was one of the easiest villains by a long shot - between him being cloaked for the first several turns, two Krakens, and a complete lack of healing or damage redirection cards until the end of the game, Parse ended up cheering on the rest of the team from her bloodied spot on the floor.

Finally, Apostate had some devious plan involving the Block, but Fanatic showed up to stop him accompanied by Setback, Absolute Zero, the Argent Adept, and Tachyon who ended up Sucker Punching Apostate to avoid having to deal with the three relics that were out.

posts.cooked:
“Aminia? What are you doing in an extradimensional prison for supervillains?” Young Legacy asked.

“Oh, uh, I’m…looking for paperclips for the office, and I got lost in the closet and ended up here?” Miss Information said.

“Well that makes sense to me, because I am extraordinarily thick,” said Young Legacy.

“Nothing at all about that story sounds suspicious to me either,” Expatriette agreed. “Did I mention I am intensely stupid?”

“Yee haw! Ride em cowboy! I’m plumb loco! Don’t touch my spurs!” were the sum of Chrono-Ranger’s thoughts.

“Uh huh. Hey, Expatriette, would you mind going to the shower room alone and helping Char find his soap? Alone? Without anyone else there to help you if he decides to set you on fire and/or poison you?” Miss Information asked.

“It would be very nice of you to accept this very straightforward request, Expatriette,” Young Legacy before being distracted by a very lickable part of the wall.

“I do spend a lot of time just plain shooting people,” Expatriette admitted, momentarily pausing in her efforts to wear her left boot as a hat. “Maybe it would feel nice to help someone who surely isn’t a psychotic murderer and is probably imprisoned in this extradimensional pocket for tax evasion.”

“Get along little dogie! Let’s giddyup back to the Ponderosa!” Chrono-Ranger said, then sat down because he was dizzy from all the spinning around he was doing while trying to bite his own ear.

Some time later, after everyone had been hit with moderate radiation burns on top of having been shot at a few times by jumpy prison guards, Young Legacy said, “You know, I’m starting to think Aminia might be a bad person.”

“My hair is falling out and I have blisters inside my organs, and I don’t know if that’s Aminia’s fault but I want to shoot someone because that’s the only method of emotional expression I know,” Expatriette said.

“I demand to see the long form birth certificate! 9/11 was an inside job! Obamacare has death panels what for killin’ your granny!” Chrono-Ranger said.

Then everyone shot Miss Information a lot and she fell down.

I really hate the Matriarch.

Dark Watch Setback, Dark Visionary, Omnitron-X, and Nightmist just went up against her. It was frigging grueling, but Setback’s Wrong Time and Place was the key to victory; just piling on all the unlucky tokens I could get my hands on to counterattack as often as possible per round, struggling to keep Setback’s HP above the brink (thank god for Innervation Ray), and finishing her off in the final round of 22 HP with 10 HP of Self Sabotage and two 2 HP draws on an Oblivion spell, all 8 of which Setback was able to bounce onto the Matriarch before the spell itself piled on the final 4 HP and killed her.

Legacy, Rook City Wraith, and Freedom Tempest got together to beat up Skinwalker Gloomweaver in the Time Cataclysm. They brought along the Naturalist because they thought it would be funny to bring him to fight zombies when his primary method of attack is to bite things. Wraith got out Throwing Knives and a Utility Belt in the first round, and Tempest got out a Grievous Hailstorm, so damage was pretty well covered, though it took forever to flip Gloomweaver because he had two relics out in the first round and after I killed them, they of course came right back out again with a Vast Following. It was for the best, though, because the extra time to beat up Gloomweaver gave Legacy time to get out a Next Evolution and a Lead from the Front to immunize the party from Gloomweaver’s various infernal attacks. In the end, though, they showed Gloomweaver the error of manifesting in a physical body in this world, because physical bodies mean high winds, lightning strikes, hail, and pointy bits of metal all hurt.

So do crocodile teeth, but I’m sure Gloomweaver took some comfort in the misery the Naturalist endured from the flavor of eating zombie meat.

Final round of the game. The Scholar (25 HP), Fanatic the Redeemer (9 HP), Dark Watch Setback (1 HP), and KNYFE (10 HP) are going up against la Capitan in the Realm of Discord. La Capitan has Siege Breaker, l’Episte, Battle Forged, the Amazing Mable, Final Breath, and Chip in play, which has reduced the heroes to the above HP totals; she has 27. Two Portal Fiends are in play with six cards in the environment trash. There is no way this is not the last round of the game. It’s time for a blitz.

The Scholar leads with “Get Out of the Way!” He inflicts 8 total points of damage, heals that much, and hits la Capitan with the backlash from Mortal Form to Energy, knocking her down to 18. Fanatic the Redeemer has a ton of cards that could inflict one or two damage, but she wisely elects to play Embolden on KNYFE and just hits la Capitan with Absolution to knock her down to 15. Dark Watch Setback plays Exceeded Expectations and activates Looking Up, putting her down to 7. Knyfe has a Prototype Servo-Gauntlet in play and Amplified Combatant (la Capitan is now down to 4), hits her with the Prototype Servo-Gauntlet’s power (down to 1), and finishes her off with an energy lance.

I think I’ve stress-sweated right through my shirt.

posts.cooked:
So the girlfriend and I ran a random game that knocked down two more of your slots.

The Chairman versus The Eternal Haka, Wraith, Omnitron-X, and Tachyon ON MARS!

Eternal Haka and Wraith needed the win.  I played Haka and Omni, she played Tachy and Wraith. 

Just how the murderous Chairman, The Operative, and a variable army of criminals managed to make it to the Wagner Mars Base is something of a mystery.  Luckily for the scientists on staff Doctor Meredith Stinson was on hand performing some infistructure upgrades with the assistance of her compatriot The Wraith.  Still vastly outnumbered and out gunned the two members of The Freedom Five were relieved when stepping out of a blinding flash was Omnitron-X!  The reformed killing machine had not come alone however,  he brought with him a powerful ally from the end of time, The Eternal Haka to turn the tide!

The match was brutal, Red Dust kept wrecking Omni and Wraith's set ups.  Haka finally managed to pull Savage Mana and we were able to start putting thugs away each round.  By the time every thug was under Savage Mana, and villainous upgrades, the heroes were on the ropes, all under 10 HP.  The Chairman had yet to flip, he and the Operative still had full health, and all the Under bosses were in play.  That's when The Chairman declared "Rook City is mine!" Which is odd, as he was on Mars, which caused two massive meteor swarms to start.  Taking cover our heroes decided to wait a few rounds heal up get massive draw hands, and have Omnitron-X, handle any pesky extra environment cards draws, withy Tachy and Wraith occasionally helping out.  

Finally the heroes were ready.  They stopped the metor swarms and unleashed the dogs of war on the under bosses finally getting the Chairman to flip.  After Haka dragged a few more Underbosses under savage mana, Tachyon, with her HUD goggles, Fleet of Foot, Lightning Reflexes, a couple copies of light speed barrage and some other things Tachyon laid down 45 points of damage her turn taking out The Chairman.  The Eternal Haka finished the fight with the Haka of Battle, sacrificing his entire hand to pump Savage Mana to 51 damage utterly destroying The Operative.

 

Thus the day... Was saved.

I’m taking a frustration break right now because I lost six games in a row, three each of randomly chosen Elemental Wrath Absolute Zero, Engine of War Bunker, Young Legacy, and Unity against Agent of Gloom Spite (never bring in that many slow build, low damage characters against Agent of Gloom Spite) and of Parse, Elemental Wrath Absolute Zero, and Dark Visionary against Baron Blade, Ermine, and Fright Train (never bring in a team of 66% deck manipulators with piddling damage potential against that many villain targets).

posts.name: JimB
posts.cooked:
I wanted to reduce the number of games left for Spite: Agent of Gloom, so I did. Random dice rolls came up with Elemental Wrath Absolute Zero and Engine of War Bunker again, as well as Expatriette and Rook City Wraith. I said some bad words but toughened up and stuck with it for reasons I cannot, in retrospect, be sure were actual reasons and not just sheer bloody-mindedness.

Spite whupped me pretty bad the first time (he has 40 HP left), and not so bad the second time (he had 4 HP left). I was resigned to failure nevertheless in the third game, but the first card he put out was a Good Samaritan, and Wraith’s Infrared Eyepiece put another Good Samaritan on top of his deck so that at the beginning of the second round, two victim cards were under the Safe House and his only drug card, the one that does damage whenever you use a power, was turned face-down again. With him unable to get any drugs turned up, the game was over in six rounds (Absolute Zero’s first played card was Impale, Bunker’s was Gatling Gun, Expatriette’s was Pride, and Wraith got out a Utility Belt and a Razor Ordinance in round two, so damage was plentiful). Everyone had at least 20 HP at the game’s end.

It bothers me that only an unlucky shuffle for Spite enabled me to beat him. I still haven’t figured out any reliable way to handle this jerk.

posts.name: JimB
posts.cooked:
I really wish I’d paid more attention to how I did it, but I checked the records of HP loss against the number of environment cards played (Freedom Tower being what it is, it serves as an excellent round counter), and…yeah. Young Legacy, Eternal Haka, Dark Watch Expatriette, Price of Freedom Wraith, and Horus just destroyed the Vengeance Five in six rounds. A first round Rampage on Haka’s part was extremely helpful, of course, as well as a couple of turns of Shock Rounds even from poor little Pride, a Grappling Hook to get rid of Blade’s Genetically Enfused Physique,* and Drawn to the Flame while four villain Ongoing cards were in play all helped…but I really have no idea how I did it.

*I like to try to picture in my head how this happened. It involves Wraith getting Blade pinned down and performing a lobotomy with the sharpest end of the grappling hook.

posts.name: JimB
posts.cooked: I got tired of always going for the villain with the most rounds left to go, so I decided to tackle a villain I haven’t played in so long I wasn’t even sure I remembered how to fight her: Kismet. Randomly determined Team Leader Tachyon, Golem Unity, Dark Watch Setback, and Greatest Legacy fought her in the Mobile Defense Platform. Between Golem Unity and Dark Watch Setback, the heroes ended up doing way more damage to themselves than Kismet did. Unity got out her Stealth Bot in the second round, so between Bee Bots and “Whoops! Sorry!” cards, the only times she had enough jinx cards in play to boost her damage above what Stealth Bot would soak, Tachyon would punch her ability to do damage right off her. Over and done with in five rounds.

posts.name: JimB
posts.cooked: Dark Watch Setback, the Argent Adept, Freedom Tempest, and Greatest Legacy had a bit of a nailbiter (everyone’s in single HP), but ultimately they beat the crap out of Cosmitron. Took forever to get Tempest a card with a power that deals damage, but Cosmitron played Sedative Flechettes in his first round and Tempest put out Healing Downpour, so everyone stayed pretty high until the last Sedative Flechettes at the bottom of Cosmitron’s deck. Setback put out some fair tons of damage, though, and Tempest would get out a one-shot damaging card now and then, so all was well.

posts.name: JimB
posts.cooked:
I really do hate Iron Legacy.

He decided to invade the Mobile Defense Platform, presumably to kill Baron Blade. Redeemer Fanatic, Visionary, Freedom Tempest, and Horus all tried to stop him. He had two damage buffs out in play from setup, an armor, and the one that gives him HP when heroes use a power. He proceeded to beat the everloving hell out of the team, inflicting at least ten points to everyone before his first card was played. Fanatic’s first play was Undaunted because she didn’t have anything better to do with her time (at least it would take care of that psychic damage); Visionary put out a Decoy Projection and tried to get Fanatic to draw an Apocalypse (didn’t happen); Tempest put out Vicious Cyclone, again for want of a better idea; Horus summoned and played his staff.

A mechanic came out of the environment deck.

Iron Legacy dealt seven more points of damage to everyone.

Fanatic threw out Divine Focus for want of anything useful to do and tried to draw Apocalypse (again, nope); Visionary had nothing to play and tried to give Fanatic an Apocalypse; Tempest dealt Iron Legacy three points from a Vicious Cyclone and five more from a Lightning Slash. Horus blasted Iron Legacy for five points, which would have flipped him, but by then I had an idea and used Horus’s power to heal Iron Legacy back up to 21.

Another mechanic came out of the environment deck.

Legacy killed Tempest and did everyone else another seven or so points of damage. Fanatic was down to 9 HP. She played Wrathful Retribution, knocking Legacy down to 2 HP. Visionary panicked and put up a Telekinetic Cocoon; Tempest rotted a bit; Horus played Imbued Flame and destroyed his staff for 5 HP, which even with Iron Legacy’s two points of healing was enough to wipe him out.

Three rounds. Yeesh.

posts.name: JimB
posts.cooked: Well, the Vengeance Five got their frigging vengeance, killing Dark Visionary, Expatriette, Redeemer Fanatic, and Freedom Tempest in the Final Wasteland. In the end, Ermine and X were the only ones left, and X was being fed a steady stream of HP while X’s Ablative Coating took care of any damage Ermine could inflict. It still took eight turns to knock off her final 5 HP, though, because she had her damnable Subtle Diversion out and all he could do was ping her with his Rocket Punch.

posts.name: JimB
posts.cooked: Miss Information did…whatever she does on the crowded streets of Megalopolis. Engine of War Bunker was there to destroy her Diversions, Dark Watch Setback was there to do that as well as inflict damage, and Rook City Wraith was there to do pretty much everything at all times because she’s awesome like that but mostly to make sure Megalopolis didn’t screw us. Because of Wraith, two police officer cards were in play tearing Miss Information down when she flipped, and their efforts were appreciated even though the Gatling Gun, the Flak Cannon, the big dummy’s fists, and even the skinny chick’s throwing knives were all doing better jobs. She fell down fast once she flipped.

posts.name: JimB
posts.cooked: Not much to say. GI Bunker, Dark Watch Nightmist, Elemental Wrath Absolute Zero, Mister Fixer, and Visionary just beat up the Vengeance Five in the Ruins of Atlantis. It was over in five rounds. The Kraken was a big help.

posts.name: Pydro
posts.cooked:
Weekend Update:

Total Matches left: 368

Hero with least number of matches left: Omnitron-X with 2.

Hero with the most matches left: EoW: Bunker and DW Mr. Fixer with 16

Villain with the least matches left: Apostate - 0,  Proletariat with 6.

Villain with the most matches left: Ambuscade and the Dreamer with 20.

posts.name: JimB
posts.cooked:
Pydro:

Ambuscade and the Dreamer with 20.

Just the Dreamer now! Dark Watch Setback, Horus, Team Leader Tachyon, and Dark Watch Nightmist just took him on in Pike Industrial Complex. Advanced Ambuscade is actually a villain to bother taking seriously; he killed Setback and Horus, though Horus was my fault for hoarding staves instead of exploding them to bring more in for HP. Setback was nothing but bad luck. Six rounds went by without him getting a card that generates unlucky tokens, and by then, well, it was too late.

It also didn’t help that Ambuscade got out two Reactive Shields and a Cloaking Device in the first two rounds, so I had to leave him invisible just to keep the DR on his Reactive Shields low enough to actually hurt them, which meant he just kept plugging away at Setback until there was no saving him. Of course Pike Industrial is just murder for everyone, though Pike isn’t quite as bad when you have Tachyon and Nightmist both fully capable of taking out environment cards.

As would be expected from a team of Tachyon and Nightmist, Ambuscade mostly killed himself. He would try to shoot someone and Tachyon would run forward, grab him, and throw him in front of the bullet like Bugs Bunny, or Nightmist would just bounce bullets back at him from her +1 Choker of Evil.

It was interesting to watch two heroes die to Ambuscade. I will have to stop making fun of him.

posts.name: Ronway
posts.cooked:
JimB:

It was interesting to watch two heroes die to Ambuscade. I will have to stop making fun of him.

Just be happy you haven't lost to him in 2 rounds. Curse you Sherriff Pratt!!

posts.name: JimB
posts.cooked:
Pydro:

Hero with least number of matches left: Omnitron-X with 2.

I want to see another black line across the grid, so I’m going to do Omnitron-X’s two remaining fights. I just did Bomber Blade in Insula Primalis with Dark Watch Mr. Fixer, Haka, X, and Nightmist; and let me tell you, Dark Watch Mr. Fixer made this kind of embarrassing to take part in. I felt bad Blade. Pipe Wrench, Grease Monkey Style, Harmony, and Obsidian Field…Blade never had a chance. Over in five rounds.

I never thought about it before, but the Dark Watch have some pretty okay teamwork going on. Between the team, there’s really no reason you shouldn’t have some piece of crap ongoing or unnecessary equipment you can’t sacrifice to Mr. Fixer.
